newsitem.title: USA: Three arrested in shooting of NY police officer.
newsitem.headline: Three arrested in shooting of NY police officer.

text.p: Three men were arrested on Friday in connection with the sniper shooting of a New York City police officer in October in front of the station house where he worked, police said.
The arrests were made as the result of information gathered during an unrelated arrest by a nearby precinct.
Police Commissioner Howard Safir said police had passed on the information to detectives of the 46th precinct in New York City's borough of the Bronx where the shooting occurred.
The three men, Jose Ortiz, 30 of Springfield, Mass, Damien Ponce, 49, and Guillermo Negron, 41, both of the Bronx are charged with attempted murder, aggravated assault and conspiracy.
Safir said Ortiz allegedly shot Captain Steven Plavnick, 47, on Oct. 19 as he got out of his car outside the precinct.

Police said at the time of the shooting they were examining whether the attack might have been in retaliation for the acquittal of police officer Francis Livoti who was cleared two weeks earlier in the choke-hold death of a young man.

At a news conference late on Friday, Safir would not say whether the shooting of Plavnick was in revenge for Livoti's acquittal. "We believe that the shooting was gang-related. The investigation is continuing," Safir said.
